docs.title: Stocktacking Access
docs.text:
• Stocktacking function is used monthly to update inventory item quantities to match actual quantities
  • Enabling stocktacking access allows users with warehouse permission to access stocktaking controls and start/end stocktaking operations
  • See 'Stocktacking Control' for more information
  • When stocktacking is active (function being used by Warehouse user), stocktacking access cannot be disabled by Warehouse Administration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Stocktaking System provides persistent global state management to control inventory operations during stocktaking periods. When stocktaking mode is active, all inventory modifications (inbound/outbound/update operations) are disabled system-wide to ensure data integrity during stock counting.

docs.title: 🔒 Persistent State Management
docs.text:
• Configuration stored in database (system_config table)
  • State survives server restarts
  • Atomic configuration updates

docs.title: 🛡️ System-wide Protection
docs.text:
• Blocks all inventory log operations during stocktaking
  • Prevents inventory updates during counting
  • API-level enforcement with clear error messages

docs.title: 👥 Administrative Control
docs.text:
• Only Admin users can start/end stocktaking
  • Full audit trail with timestamps and user tracking
  • Real-time status monitoring

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE "system_config" (
    "config_key" system_config_key PRIMARY KEY,
    "config_value" text NOT NULL,
    "updated_at" timestamp DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    "updated_by" integer REFERENCES "user"("id")
);

docs.title: Configuration Keys
docs.text:
• stocktaking_mode: 'true' or 'false'
  • stocktaking_start_time: ISO timestamp
  • stocktaking_started_by: User ID
  • maintenance_mode: Reserved for future use

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /api/system/stocktaking/status - Get current status
  • POST /api/system/stocktaking/start - Start stocktaking (Admin only)
  • POST /api/system/stocktaking/end - End stocktaking (Admin only)

docs.title: Starting Stocktaking
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Dashboard → Admin Portal
  2. Find the "Stocktaking Control" panel
  3. Click "Start Stocktaking"
  4. Confirm in the modal dialog

What happens: - All inventory operations are immediately blocked - Current timestamp and user are recorded - Status becomes ACTIVE with red badge

docs.title: Monitoring Status
docs.text: The Stocktaking Control panel shows: - Current status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE) - Start time and initiating user - Warning about disabled operations - Real-time status updates

docs.title: Ending Stocktaking
docs.text:
1. Click "End Stocktaking" button
  2. Confirm in the modal dialog

What happens: - Inventory operations are re-enabled - Configuration is cleared - Status becomes INACTIVE with green badge

docs.title: During Normal Operations
docs.text:
• All inventory functions work normally
  • Inbound/outbound logging available
  • Inventory updates permitted

docs.title: During Stocktaking
docs.text:
• Blocked Operations:
  • Inventory log entries (/api/inventory/log/add)
  • Inventory updates (/api/inventory/item) (PATCH)

  • Any other inventory modifications

  • Available Operations:

  • View inventory (read-only)
  • Search items
  • View reports
  • Non-inventory functions

docs.title: Error Messages
docs.text:
When attempting blocked operations:

"Inventory log operations is not allowed during stocktaking. 
Please complete stocktaking first."

docs.title: System Configuration Service
docs.text:
File: src/lib/server/system-config.ts

Key functions: - isStocktakingActive() - Check current status - startStocktaking(userId) - Begin stocktaking mode - endStocktaking(userId) - End stocktaking mode - ensureStocktakingNotActive(operation) - Middleware check

docs.title: Protected APIs
docs.text:
APIs with stocktaking protection: - Inventory log operations - Inventory updates - Future: Order processing, stock adjustments

Protection pattern:

await ensureStocktakingNotActive('Operation name');

docs.title: Frontend Components
docs.text:
• StocktakingControl.svelte - Admin control panel
  • Real-time status updates
  • Confirmation modals for safety

docs.title: Stocktaking Workflow
docs.text:
1. Preparation Phase
  2. Notify all staff of upcoming stocktaking
  3. Complete pending inventory transactions

  4. Generate pre-stocktaking reports

  5. Stocktaking Phase

  6. Admin starts stocktaking mode
  7. Physical counting begins
  8. All inventory changes blocked

  9. Count discrepancies recorded separately

  10. Completion Phase

  11. Physical count verified
  12. Adjustments prepared (offline)
  13. Admin ends stocktaking mode
  14. Adjustments applied to system

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• Only Admin role can control stocktaking
  • All configuration changes are audited
  • Database-level persistence prevents bypassing
  • Clear error messages prevent confusion

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Graceful degradation when database unavailable
  • Clear user feedback for blocked operations
  • Automatic status refresh in admin panel
  • Comprehensive logging for troubleshooting

docs.title: Database Migration
docs.text:
Run the migration script:

# Apply the migration
npm run db:migrate

docs.title: Required Files
docs.text:
• src/lib/shared/system-config.ts - Type definitions
  • src/lib/server/system-config.ts - Core service
  • src/lib/components/dashboard/StocktakingControl.svelte - UI component
  • src/routes/api/system/stocktaking/** - API endpoints
  • drizzle/0003_add_system_config_table.sql - Database schema

docs.title: API Integration
docs.text:
Add to protected endpoints:

import { ensureStocktakingNotActive } from '$lib/server/system-config';

// In your API handler:
await ensureStocktakingNotActive('Operation description');

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Q: Stocktaking won't start - Check user has Admin permissions - Verify database connectivity - Check server logs for errors

Q: Operations still blocked after ending stocktaking - Refresh admin panel status - Check database system_config table - Restart application if needed

Q: Status not updating in UI - Click "Refresh" button in admin panel - Check browser network requests - Verify API endpoint accessibility

docs.title: Database Queries
docs.text:
Check current configuration:

SELECT * FROM system_config;

Manually end stocktaking (emergency):

UPDATE system_config 
SET config_value = 'false' 
WHERE config_key = 'stocktaking_mode';

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The new stocktaking system uses a two-tier control structure: 1. Admin: Controls access to stocktaking functionality 2. Warehouse: Executes the actual stocktaking operations

docs.title: 1. Admin Enables Stocktaking (Admin Role Only)
docs.text:
Location: Dashboard → Admin Portal → Stocktaking Access

Actions: - Toggle switch to "Enable" stocktaking for Warehouse - System shows status: ENABLED (green badge) - Warehouse users can now see Stocktaking Control panel

docs.title: 2. Warehouse Starts Stocktaking (Warehouse Role)
docs.text:
Location: Dashboard → Stocktaking Control (only visible when enabled)

Actions: - Click "Start Stocktaking" button - Confirm in modal dialog - System immediately blocks all inventory operations - Status shows: ACTIVE (red badge)

docs.title: 3. Physical Stocktaking Process
docs.text: During Active Period: - ✅ Available: View inventory, search, reports - ❌ Blocked: All inventory changes (inbound/outbound/updates) - 📊 Status: Real-time display of start time and user

docs.title: 4. Warehouse Ends Stocktaking
docs.text: Actions: - Click "End Stocktaking" button - Confirm in modal dialog - System automatically: - Re-enables inventory operations - Disables stocktaking functionality access - Hides Stocktaking Control panel from Warehouse

docs.title: 5. Auto-Reset to Initial State
docs.text: Result: - Warehouse users no longer see Stocktaking Control - Admin must re-enable for next stocktaking cycle - System returns to normal operations

docs.title: Access Control

docs.title: State Protection
docs.text:
• Cannot disable while stocktaking is active
  • Database persistence through server restarts
  • Clear error messages for invalid operations

docs.title: Configuration Keys
docs.text:
stocktaking_enabled: 'true'/'false'  - Admin controls access
stocktaking_mode: 'true'/'false'     - Active stocktaking state
stocktaking_start_time: ISO timestamp
stocktaking_started_by: User ID

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
POST /api/system/stocktaking/enable   - Admin only
POST /api/system/stocktaking/disable  - Admin only
POST /api/system/stocktaking/start    - Warehouse only (when enabled)
POST /api/system/stocktaking/end      - Warehouse only
GET  /api/system/stocktaking/status   - All authorized users

docs.title: Improved Security

docs.title: Better Control

This workflow ensures secure, controlled stocktaking operations with clear separation of administrative and operational responsibilities.

docs.title: Timesheet and Expense Sheet System Documentation
docs.text:
The timesheet and expense sheet system allows for users to handle submitting their working hours and work expenses, and for system administrators to manage projects and roles, and review submission sheets from users.

For a getting started guide for users, go here.

For a getting started guide for administrators, go here.

docs.title: Introduction and Navigation
docs.text:
Users can access the timesheet and expense sheet system using the Employee Portal button in the navigation bar on the inventory system dashboard page, or the /project1 route.

From the Dashboard Hub, users can see basic statistics on their total pending and rejected submissions.

Under Quick Actions, users can access the pages to view and submit their timesheets and expense sheets.

docs.title: Timesheets
docs.text:
From the Timesheet page, users can access their controls for managing and viewing their timesheet submissions.

Under the different tab pages, users can create a New Sheet, View Draft, View Pending, View Rejected, and View Approved.

docs.title: New Sheet
docs.text:
In the New Sheet tab, users submit their timesheet submissions.

Users can save their current timesheet submission as a draft with the Save as Draft button, and can submit their current timesheet as a pending submission for an administrator to review with the Submit Time Sheet button.

When the user attempts to save as a draft or submit to an administrator for review, the timesheet submission must first be valid, so every added row must have all required fields entered.

When a timesheet is successfully saved as a draft, the tab will be switched to the View Draft tab and set the newly created timesheet as the currently selected timesheet. When a timesheet is successfully submitted for review, the tab will be switched to the View Pending tab and set the newly created timesheet as the currently selected timesheet.

Users can add multiple rows to a timesheet with the Add Row button. There is no limit for how many rows may be added to a timesheet.

A row represents a continuous time frame, so timesheets may contain multiple rows with the same date (ex. the user enters a row for their working hours before their lunch break, and another row for their working hours after their lunch break).

Users can remove a row using the red button with the trash-can icon at the end of the row.

docs.title: Timesheet Supervisor
docs.text:
The Timesheet Supervisor is the administrator that the user will request to review their timesheet, and must be a user with valid administrator permissions.

The Timesheet Supervisor is distinct from the Supervisor field, and does not need to be the same administrator.

docs.title: Date
docs.text: The respective date of the timesheet row.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: The related project of the timesheet row. Projects are created by administrators, and have roles assigned to them.

docs.title: Role
docs.text: The related role of the timesheet row. Roles are created by administrators, and are assigned under a project. Users must first select a Project before they can select a role.

docs.title: Supervisor
docs.text:
The related supervisor of the timesheet row.

The Supervisor is distinct from the Timesheet Supervisor field, and does not need to be the same administrator.

docs.title: Time In
docs.text:
The respective start time of the timesheet row. When entered with a Time Out, the Hours will automatically be calculated.

The Hours calculated by the range may not exceed 24 hours, so the user must create another row if they wish to log mo re than 24 hours for a time frame.

docs.title: Time Out
docs.text:
The respective end time of the timesheet row. When entered with a Time In, the Hours will automatically be calculated.

The Hours calculated by the range may not exceed 24 hours, so the user must create another row if they wish to log mo re than 24 hours for a time frame.

docs.title: Non-Billable
docs.text: Marks whether the timesheet row is a billable time frame.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The user may add a description to a timesheet row to add clarifications and details, or leave a note for the administrator to read during review.

docs.title: Per Diem
docs.text:
Marks whether the timesheet row is a daily allowance paid to employees to cover expenses incurred while traveling for work. Users can mark more than one per diem field in a timesheet row.

The label markings are as follows:

  • B – Breakfast
  • L – Lunch
  • S – Supper
  • I – Incidentals

docs.title: View Draft
docs.text: The View Draft tab displays the user's existing timesheet drafts, and allows the user to search and select a timesheet draft to edit and update.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Clicking on a timesheet draft in the table opens a modal to view the timesheet draft details. The Select button in the modal selects the timesheet draft for editing. Clicking the View Draft tab will set the view back to displaying the user's timesheet drafts.

The UI for editing the timesheet draft is the same as in the New Sheet tab.

The Delete button will delete the currently selected timesheet draft.

The Save Draft button will update the currently selected timesheet draft with the newly edited values.

The Submit Draft will submit the current selected timesheet draft for review from the administrator, and change the current tab view to View Pending with the current timesheet as the selected timesheet.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Timesheet drafts can be searched using their Timesheet ID if you happen to already know it, or their timestamp that they were created at.

Timestamps are formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ (etc. 2025-08-07T20:36:33.750Z), and search completion results may not show up until the YYYY-MM are entered into the search box (etc. 2025-08).

docs.title: View Pending
docs.text: The View Pending tab displays the user's pending timesheets for review from the administrator, and allows the user to search and select a pending timesheet to edit and update.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Clicking on a pending timesheet in the table opens a modal to view the pending timesheet details. The Select button in the modal selects the pending timesheet for editing. Clicking the View Draft tab will set the view back to displaying the user's pending timesheet.

The UI for editing the pending timesheet is the same as in the New Sheet tab.

The Delete button will delete the currently selected pending timesheet.

The Save as Draft will remove the current selected pending timesheet from review and change it to a timesheet draft, and set the current tab view to View Draft with the current timesheet as the selected timesheet.

The Update Submission button will update the currently selected pending timesheet with the newly edited values.

docs.text:
From the Expense Sheet page, users can access their controls for managing and viewing their expense sheet submissions.

Under the different tab pages, users can create a New Sheet, View Draft, View Pending, View Rejected, and View Approved.

docs.title: New Sheet
docs.text:
In the New Sheet tab, users submit their expense sheet submissions.

Users can save their current expense sheet submission as a draft with the Save as Draft button, and can submit their current expense sheet as a pending submission for an administrator to review with the Submit Expense Sheet button.

When the user attempts to save as a draft or submit to an administrator for review, the expense sheet submission must first be valid, so every added row must have all required fields entered.

When a expense sheet is successfully saved as a draft, the tab will be switched to the View Draft tab and set the newly created expense sheet as the currently selected expense sheet. When a expense sheet is successfully submitted for review, the tab will be switched to the View Pending tab and set the newly created expense sheet as the currently selected expense sheet.

Users can add multiple rows to a expense sheet with the Add Row button. There is no limit for how many rows may be added to a expense sheet.

A row represents a single expense, so expense sheets may contain multiple rows with the same date.

Users can remove a row using the red button with the trash-can icon at the end of the row.

docs.text:

docs.title: Supervisor
docs.text:
The related supervisor of the expense sheet row.

The Supervisor is distinct from the Expense Supervisor field, and does not need to be the same administrator.

docs.title: Billable
docs.text: Marks whether the expense sheet row is a billable expense.

docs.title: Name
docs.text: The respective name of the expense.

docs.title: Payment Type
docs.text: The respective payment type of the expense.

docs.title: Expense Type
docs.text: The respective payment type of the expense. The Car Rental and Mileage expense types require extra fields.

docs.title: Car Rental
docs.text: The KM In and KM Out specify the kilometers into the journey and out made by the Rental Company.

docs.title: Mileage
docs.text: The KM In and KM Out specify the kilometers into the journey, and are used alongside the Rate to automatically compute and fill out the Amount field as amount = (km_out - km_in) * rate. The amount can still be manually entered in later.

docs.title: Amount
docs.text: The respective amount cost of the expense.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The user may add a description to a expense sheet row to add clarifications and details, or leave a note for the administrator to read during review.

docs.title: Receipts
docs.text:
The user may upload receipts or files as proof/evidence of their expense, if required by the administrator.

Supported file types include:

  • pdf
  • jpg
  • png
  • docx
  • xlsx
  • txt

docs.title: Introduction and Navigation
docs.text:
Administrators can access the timesheet and expense sheet system using the Employee Portal button in the navigation bar on the inventory system dashboard page, or the /project1 route.

Under Quick Actions, administrators can access the pages to Review Submissions and change Admin Settings.

docs.title: Review Submissions
docs.text:
From the Review Submissions page, administrators can choose to review and approve Timesheets or Expense Sheets assigned to them from users who have specified them as the Timesheet Supervisor or Expense Supervisor in their sheet submissions.

In the respective Timesheet and Expense Sheet review pages, administrators may click on a sheet entry in the table to view its details and row entries.

Clicking on the Reject and Approve next to a sheet entry in the table will open a modal to confirm the action, and the administrator may optionally leave comments for the user to read.

docs.title: Admin Settings
docs.text:
The administrator may manage Projects and project Roles through the Admin Settings page. Projects are listed under the Project Numbers table, and Roles are listed under the Project Roles table.

Under Actions in the table, the blue edit button will open a modal similar to the Add New modal where administrators can edit and save changes, and the red delete button will delete the entry.

docs.title: Project Numbers
docs.text: New Projects can be added with the Add New button, which will open a modal and prompt the administrator to input the required fields for a new project. Changes will be applied when the Save Changes button is pressed.

docs.title: Project Name
docs.text: The respective name of the project.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The respective description of the project.

docs.title: Start Date
docs.text: The respective start date of the project.

docs.title: End Date
docs.text: The respective start date of the project.

docs.title: Assign Roles
docs.text: The administrator may assign or unassign existing roles to a project. When roles are unassigned from a project they are deleted, and when existing roles are assigned to a project a new role is created that is mapped to the project when changes are applied. Changes will be applied when the Save Changes button is pressed.

docs.title: Project Roles
docs.text: New Roles can be added with the Add New button, which will open a modal and prompt the administrator to input the required fields for a new role.

docs.title: Project
docs.text: The Project that the current role is assigned to. A role may only be assigned to one existing project, but multiple roles with the same name may be assigned to different projects.

docs.title: Role Name
docs.text: The respective name of the role.
